cards.text: Joseph's brothers have come back to Egypt with Benjamin, their youngest brother, and feasted with Joseph, ruler over the land (Genesis 42:6; 43:15, 34). They STILL have no idea he's Joseph, the brother they once threw into a pit (Genesis 37:24; 42:8). Now Joseph tells his steward to fill the men's sacks with as much food as they can carry.

cards.question: Joseph also tells the steward to put each man's ___ back in the mouth of his sack.

cards.text: Then Joseph adds one more thing, just for the youngest one's sack. That's Benjamin, Joseph's own mother's son (Genesis 43:29).

cards.question: What does Joseph have the steward slip into Benjamin's sack?

cards.text: At daybreak the brothers head home with their donkeys, and they're not far from the city when Joseph sends his steward chasing after them. It's like walking out of a store and the alarm goes BEEP, and you have NO idea why.

cards.question: Joseph gives the steward a question to throw at the brothers when he catches them. What is it?

answers.text: Why have you repaid good with evil
Why did you leave before the dawn
Why did you lie about your brother

cards.text: The steward is also told to say this is the cup his master drinks from and uses for divination, and then, "What you have done is wicked!" He catches up and says it all, just like Joseph told him.

cards.question: True or false: When the steward accuses them, the brothers admit they took the cup.
To prove they're honest men, what do the brothers remind the steward of?

answers.text: They brought back the silver they found
They never once left the steward's sight
They swore an oath before Pharaoh himself

cards.text: Then the brothers make the steward an offer: whoever is found with the cup must die, and the rest of them will become slaves.

cards.question: True or false: The steward agrees that if the cup turns up, the rest of the brothers will become slaves too.

cards.text: Every brother lowers his sack to the ground and opens it FAST. I bet nobody's breathing.

cards.question: The steward searches the sacks one at a time, starting with the ___ brother.

cards.text: One sack… the next… the next… and there's the cup, in Benjamin's sack. The brothers tear their clothes.

cards.question: True or false: After the cup turns up, the brothers all go back to the city.

cards.text: Not one of them says, "Well, it was nice knowing you, Benjamin." They ALL fall to the ground before Joseph, who declares, "What is this deed you have done?"

cards.question: Judah, one of the brothers, doesn't argue or make excuses. What does he say God has done?

answers.text: Sent the famine as a warning
Sent the steward to test them

cards.question: Judah tells Joseph they are now his slaves. Who does Judah include?

answers.text: All the brothers along with Benjamin
Only the oldest of the brothers

cards.text: Joseph answers, "Far be it from me to do this." Only the man found with the cup will be his slave, and the rest of them may go back to their father in peace.

Then Judah steps right up to Joseph and says, "Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself." Friend, that's like walking straight into the CEO's office without an appointment.
Judah starts at the beginning: Joseph once asked if they had a father or a brother. They told him about an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age.

cards.question: They also told Joseph that the younger brother's full brother, from the same mother, is ___.
True or false: When Joseph told them to bring their younger brother down, the brothers warned that if the boy left his father, his father would die.

cards.text: But Joseph said unless the younger brother came down, they would not see his face again. Back home they passed that on, and then their father said, "Go back and buy us some food."

cards.question: True or false: The brothers told their father they could go see the man without their younger brother.

cards.text: Then Judah repeats what their father, Jacob, said to them. It starts, "You know that my wife bore me two sons."

cards.question: Jacob says one of his two sons was gone. What did Jacob say had happened to him?

answers.text: He'd been lost in the desert

cards.question: Jacob says if they take Benjamin too and harm comes to him, what will that do to Jacob?

answers.text: Send him to his grave in sorrow
Make him leave Canaan for good
Turn him against all of his sons

cards.text: Judah lays it out: their father's life is wrapped up in the boy's life. If Jacob sees the boy isn't with them, he will die.

cards.question: Then Judah tells Joseph something Judah did back home with his father. What was it?

answers.text: He paid for the grain himself
He promised to bring more grain

cards.text: If he didn't bring the boy home, Judah said he'd bear the guilt before his father all his life. Friend, Judah didn't just make a promise, he CO-SIGNED for his little brother.

cards.question: So here it comes, Judah's big ask. What does Judah beg Joseph to do?

answers.text: Keep Judah as a slave in place of the boy
Let the brothers buy the boy back later
Take double the silver in place of the boy

cards.question: Judah asks how he can go back to his father without the boy. He says he could not bear to see the ___ that would overwhelm his father.

cards.text: And Judah, the same brother who once said to sell Joseph (Genesis 37:26-27), stops right there, with Joseph's answer still hanging in the air. Stick with me, friend, because this story is NOT done.
